structured_output.justification: The contract fixes the fuel surcharge at 12% of the freight charge (base freight plus express premium where applicable) per §3. Falcon's own credit note FALCON-CN-01 admits the FF-8005 line was invoiced with a 15% fuel surcharge "in error" and states the contractual rate is 12%, issuing a credit for the difference. This is exactly the kind of correction §8 contemplates a credit note making, and it corroborates the already-detected line-level pricing delta on FALCON-2026-07A/FF-8005 rather than introducing a new, separate dispute amount. Since the credit note's stated amount matches the independently computed line-level delta one-for-one, there is no additional money to count here — the underlying billing error is real and should be disputed at the line level, and this finding simply confirms that conclusion using the carrier's own admission.

memo_narrative.what_happened: Falcon issued credit note FALCON-CN-01 against invoice FALCON-2026-07A for consignment FF-8005, admitting the fuel surcharge was billed at 15% instead of the contractual 12% and crediting the difference.
memo_narrative.why: Per §3 of the Falcon contract, the fuel surcharge is fixed at 12% of the freight charge; Falcon's own credit note confirms the original line was overbilled, corroborating the line-level pricing discrepancy already flagged on this invoice.
memo_narrative.recommended_action: Confirm the credit note (already issued by Falcon) is applied against the FF-8005 line and reflected in the next remittance; no separate dispute action is needed since the amount is already accounted for at the line level.
